brief: THE BET, and the batch's rung-4b move. The river is 13 columns of flat WATER (RIVER_X0 114 .. RIVER_X1 127) meeting the quay's SIDE and the towpath at a pixel boundary, and nothing grows in the shallows. Add ONE new tile constant and ONE new species: a REED tile in the shallow margins — the west edge against the quay, the east edge against the towpath, and the eyot's rim — and rushes (or yellow iris) as the next entry in SPECIES, growing on the same bed CA the beds already use, so it comes and goes with the season and leans in the wind. The census must MOVE, and that is the point: expect tileKinds 144 -> 153 and speciesKinds 108 -> 117 (nine sample blocks x one new kind — check that arithmetic against census.mjs before you trust it; GLASS at #116 is the worked example). A season or an evening does not clear mapFlat; only a spatial change does. A 150-300 line diff is expected and welcome — take the swing.
successLooksLike: From the wide shot the river no longer meets its banks at a line: a fringe stands IN the water along the margins and round the eyot, green in summer, brown and bent in winter, leaning when it blows. tileKinds and speciesKinds both move in the census, and the entry says by how much and against which baseline.
avoid: Keep reeds out of the boat channel (x 116.5-121.5), off the deck rows (DECK_Y0 30 .. DECK_Y1 32), clear of MILL_WHEEL (126.35, 21.3, r 1.25) and off the punt berths and landings — #154 has just cleared that whole track and a reed bed may not re-block it: probes/punt.mjs and punt-track.mjs must still exit 0. Do NOT extend GW or WH; the grid is full and growing WH moves every hard-coded row in 13,900 lines. And `water` reads 8784 in the last six runlog rows while the census gate reads COLLAPSE, not delta — decide up front whether a REED cell is still water to the census (it is shallow water, not land); if the class changes, re-pin with `census.mjs --save-baseline` and SAY SO in the entry.
